figures.title: Graphical abstract · Conceptual precursor/route-to-spinel overview
figures.summary: The original graphical abstract summarizes the proposed coordination-dependent nucleation pathways. It contrasts octahedral zinc at high metal-to-hydroxide ratio with a ZnO reservoir at low ratio. The cartoon is an author mechanism, not measured molecular geometry or a separate synthesis specimen.

figures.title: Figure 1 · Literature ZnAl2O4, ZnO and AlOOH structures
figures.summary: The three literature structure drawings show ZnAl2O4 spinel, ZnO and AlOOH. Orange and green polyhedra represent aluminum and zinc coordination; hydrogen is shown as white spheres. These reference depictions do not supply newly measured coordinates for the current samples.

figures.title: Figure 2 · D3 Zn-only short-range PDF and cluster comparisons
figures.summary: The D3 zinc-nitrate solution at room temperature is fitted with octahedral zinc and nitrate contributions. The original PDF, model and reference-cluster curves remain intact. Broad longer-distance features and unknown protonation do not identify one fully resolved molecular species.

figures.title: Figure 5 · Author-proposed high/low M/OH formation pathways
figures.summary: This proposed formation pathway connects aluminum dimers to tetrahedral zinc. At high M/OH, zinc must recoordinate from an octahedral precursor, while at low M/OH it is released from ZnO. The drawing expresses a mechanistic interpretation and leaves protonation, rates and exact intermediates unresolved.

intuition.title: Coordination and impurity-mediated formation
intuition.summary: The authors propose that aluminum dimers can connect with tetrahedrally coordinated zinc to nucleate spinel. At high M/OH, zinc recoordination may delay this process and favor AlOOH; at low M/OH, ZnO dissolution supplies zinc and may leave residual ZnO. Heating history changes impurity formation and consumption. These explanations are source interpretations, with the contradictory conclusion wording preserved.

general_background.title: Microwave coupling and heating
general_background.summary: Microwave fields couple to materials through their electrical response and can heat different parts of a reaction mixture differently. Polarization and mobile charges dissipate field energy, so heating depends on the liquid, dissolved species and other absorbing materials.
